attribution.note: Zitron's own words, in his own closing analysis on his newsletter.

semantics.note: A retrospective observation about reported annual losses. 'Appear to be' describes what the figures he just reported show. It is not a probability or confidence hedge about a future outcome, so the claim is scoreable. The sustainability clause is opinion and is correctly left out.

contract.note: The speaker supplied the measure himself: the headline net loss attributable, $38.53B. Comparing 2024 with 2025 on that basis, and reading 'dramatic' as a rise of several times, is an ordinary reading. The adjusted-basis caveat is correctly flagged but does not apply, because no adjusted 2024 figure exists.

evidence.note: FT-verified audited figures, relayed in a dated news report: net loss went from about $5B in 2024 to about $39B in 2025, roughly 7.8 times. Same company, metric and calendar basis.

Most of the increase was a one-time non-cash restructuring charge, and the adjusted 2025 loss was about $8B. This is a different basis from the contract's metric, so it limits the operational reading but does not contradict the claim.

A second outlet confirms the FT's adjusted loss of about $8B and repeats the headline figures. The adjusted figure is on a different basis; the parts relaying Zitron's own figures are not independent.

reviews.rationale: Independent FT-verified audited figures show OpenAI's net loss rose about 7.8 times, from about $5B in 2024 to about $39B in 2025. That meets the contract's test of a rise of several times. Most of the rise was a one-time non-cash charge (the adjusted 2025 loss was about $8B), but that is a different basis from the headline net loss the speaker cited, and no adjusted 2024 figure exists to compare against.
